root_cause_label: Agent used deprecated cryptography library API causing a DeprecationWarning in check_cert.py output that the validator flagged as failure
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent created check_cert.py using the deprecated cert.not_valid_after attribute, observed the resulting CryptographyDeprecationWarning at step 17, yet ignored it and claimed successful completion without fixing the output format.
t_err_evidence: At step 16 the agent writes /app/check_cert.py using cert.not_valid_after (a deprecated property) instead of cert.not_valid_after_utc, embedding a design choice that will produce a CryptographyDeprecationWarning in stdout on every run.
t_commit_evidence: At step 17 the deprecation warning appears in output; the agent notes 'benign deprecation warning' and does not fix it. At step 18 all tasks are marked done, locking in the broken output format with no further remediation attempted.
t_surface_evidence: Step 17 terminal output contains: '/app/check_cert.py:35: CryptographyDeprecationWarning: Properties that return a naive datetime object have been deprecated. Please switch to not_valid_after_utc.' — the first observable signal that the script's output is non-conformant.
trigger_explanation: The agent explicitly saw the CryptographyDeprecationWarning at step 17 and its own analysis noted it was 'benign', but the validator treats extra warning output as a failure. The agent had the information needed to fix the issue but dismissed it and proceeded to claim success.
forewarning_evidence: Step 17 output includes 'CryptographyDeprecationWarning: Properties that return a naive datetime object have been deprecated. Please switch to not_valid_after_utc.' — unexpected warning text in stdout before t_commit at step 18.
